newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open up, SIA falls on results.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open up, SIA falls on results.

text.p: Singapore stocks opened slightly firmer on Monday in a continuation of last week's upward trend, but shares in the national carrier Singapore Airlines (SIA) fell after disappointing half-year results.
By 0145 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 4.20 points higher at 2,081.40.
SIA's foreign tranche was four percent, or 60 cents, lower at Singapore $13.40.
Earlier on Monday, SIA reported a bottom-of-consensus 7.2 percent rise in net profit to S$560.5 million for the six months to September 30, 1996.
SIA's operating profit fell 11.4 percent to S$467.6 million, reflecting a fall in yields.
Newly-listed Guangzhou Investment Co, the Hong Kong-based trading arm of China's Guangzhou municipality, was untraded by 0145 GMT. Its 61.2 million shares were floated at HK$2.555 each.
The most active share was marine group Labroy, which saw its shares rise two cents to S$1.14 on 1.87 million shares.
Dealers were modestly bullish on the immediate prospects for the stock market. One chartist said he expected the STII to test and pull back from around the 2,100 level early this week.
